approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a persistent tree of molecular graph edits and directly buys newly reached frontier molecules. Accepted scores update only the traversed occurrences, retaining their completed count, sum, maximum and pending count. Selection borrows peak returns and exploration density from structurally similar eligible siblings. After a strict accepted improvement it starts a fresh episode from the current incumbent and the incumbent immediately before that feedback batch, in that order, using each original accepted receipt as cached context. The two roots compete under the same shared-value and shared-density rule; deeper paths keep their own exact return records.
approach.novelty: Remove only peak-value borrowing between the two promoted roots: each root competes using its own best accepted return while completed and pending exploration densities remain shared. This separates the value consumer left unresolved by the sibling that removed root value and both densities together. It also differs from the deeper value-only removal on the single-root composition. The hypothesis is that root value transfer distorts competition between the two actual origins; removing that transfer may improve purchased search while preserving shared exploration. The earlier failed benefit prediction for adding the second origin remains unchanged.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is the post-promotion virtual-root selector consuming a sibling-weighted peak instead of each origin's own receipt-backed peak, coupled to separately shared exploration density. The complete Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 has mean 0.4809700595412967 (population SD 0.025313161830483537), 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases and a refuted membership benefit prediction; its paired -0.018526255130948004 is against its own code Parent, not the formal Anchor. Removing root value and both densities together in sibling n-51af92d7316d improves this Parent by 0.03409217374872133, but two cells provide essentially the net gain and value is not separately identified. The frozen exact Parent-state own-peak replay changes 1,325/3,715 promoted-root choices in 14/15 cells, with 1,281 actual accepted paths traversing changed choices; the no-promotion median_2 seed-0 cell remains zero exposure. Sources: policy/scratch/search_policy-ef020d29d984/action-audit-summary.json, policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01/evidence-manifest.json (enumerating every exact per-cell audit, underlying log and trajectory, all Parent summaries and run logs, and their content hashes) and nodes/n-51af92d7316d/analysis.json. The deeper value-only loss of 0.012311732571151349 in n-174737d3e83d (nodes/n-174737d3e83d/analysis.json) is a direct condition boundary: it used deeper consumers and a different, single-root Parent. Passive replay establishes exposure, not alternate outcomes or expected utility.

The registered result can answer only the conditional promoted-root value contribution question on this finite Search panel.

hypothesis: Conditional removal of off-diagonal peak-value influence at exactly episode > 0 and parent_id == 0 on code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8. For each eligible root i, keep K_ij, D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j, B_i=sum_{j:N_j>0} K_ij*N_j*M_j and S_i=sum_j K_ij*W_j exactly as inherited. The passive code-Parent exploitation is B_i/D_i for D_i>0, otherwise the inherited neutral default. Active exploitation becomes M_i for N_i>0, otherwise that same neutral default. M_i remains the maximum of the unchanged normalized rewards on actual accepted occurrence-route receipts, with earliest attaining receipt identity. Exploration remains beta*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D_i+P_i)) when D_i+P_i>0; otherwise bonus and index remain None and shared zero-started priority remains active. Choose the maximum of (D_i+P_i==0, active exploitation + bonus or the inherited zero index sentinel, -occurrence_id), preserving exact original arithmetic, eligible order and ties. At episode == 0 or parent_id != 0 the active policy remains the original shared peak law. This replaces one statistical data dependency and retains both origins and their lifecycle; it does not validate or retune the refuted membership intervention.

finding_summary.headline: Root-value removal reached paid search and improved mean score, while late progress weakened
finding_summary.insights: The result supports a harmful conditional contribution from peak-value borrowing between promoted roots when shared completed and pending exploration density remain active. It answers this value-consumer question without revising the earlier result for adding a second root or assigning the same sign to deeper sharing. The allocation shifted strongly: current-origin purchases increased from 1,894 to 2,795, preceding-origin purchases fell from 1,686 to 785, and 29 preceding origins received no descendant purchase. Those associations do not prove that allocating more to the current root caused the gain, and passive alternatives have no purchased outcome. Full gain also telescopes to endpoints, so it is not independent confirmation. The retained method still shows limited late conversion and increasingly similar output: fragment-excluded similarity was 0.2020 over the full stream and 0.2532 late, versus the Parent’s 0.1976 and 0.2416. Distinct typed-scaffold counts summed within sessions fell from 2,044 to 1,898; oversized molecules increased from 244 to 289, alongside 306 small fragments. The chemistry report shows useful ring, amine and carbonyl relationships in upper-scoring structures, but inconsistent preservation of these relationships during size and topology changes. A graph proposal operator that preserves useful local chemistry while rearranging scaffolds, or a search scheme that sustains exploration across accepted neighborhoods, could address that observed limitation. This is evidence of local refinement and incomplete structural coverage, not proof of scaffold collapse or a specific operator’s fault. The result establishes neither reliable generalization nor the value of remaining density consumers. Exclusive candidate time, controlled historical timing, empirical random-state invariance and trusted task safety remain unmeasured. No new literature element was adopted; the registered internal continuation was a substantive consumer change using capabilities already present in the Parent.
finding_summary.results: The intended change executed with no detected boundary, formula or receipt-accounting violation. Own and shared exploitation differed on all 7,484 promoted-root rows. It changed 2,469 of 3,742 root choices; 2,364 of 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules traversed a changed choice, including 1,329 of 2,175 late purchases. All switches favored the current incumbent over the preceding incumbent. Fourteen of fifteen sessions were exposed; the remaining session never promoted and retained an identical trajectory. Mean final score rose from 0.480970 to 0.500149, a gain of 0.019179. All three seed means improved, but eight task/seed endpoints improved, six fell and one was unchanged. Full incumbent-increment mass rose from 4.087169 to 4.374849, while late mass fell from 0.865601 to 0.843897 and late strict improvements fell from 46 to 38. The formal Anchor mean remained 0.607030, leaving a 0.106882 deficit and its separate improvement target unmet.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich indoles, amines and fused heterocycles coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, size extremes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This is an output assessment of n-fc3b91c9623a versus published code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 on the complete frozen Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, at the stated epoch-1 profile and batch size ten. The frozen context separately states child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectory files exist. No task or paired comparison is missing. All 4500 accepted rows per side were inspected; descriptor denominators are the 4350 optimizer proposals, excluding the 150 fixed initial rows and any cached contexts. These are accepted proposals, not a census of rejected or unpurchased candidates. The Child generates indole-related carbonyl compounds, fused N/O/S heterocycles, aromatic rings carrying saturated amines, nitrogen-rich diones, partly saturated polycycles and oxygen/amino cages. It has 3905 ring-bearing and 3288 aromatic-atom-bearing proposals, versus Parent 3918 and 3373. Aromatic-atom presence is not identical to aromatic-ring presence. Frozen digest ring-closure-token rates are 0.8552–0.9356 and aromatic-token rates 0.3977–0.8839; these are string-presence rates, not atom fractions or RDKit descriptors. The diversity judgement describes many distinct graph structures across the panel, while individual upper-score neighborhoods are visibly related. Child heavy atoms span 1–114 with median 26; Parent spans 1–117 with median 26. Full Child tails are 306 below six and 289 above fifty, versus Parent 319 and 244. Late optimizer ordinals 146–290 contain 2175 molecules per side, with Child tails 143/179 and Parent 170/141 in the same order. Thus fewer fragments coexist with more oversized assemblies; neither a universal useful size nor uniform improvement is established. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold panel unions are Child 1684/1188 and Parent 1837/1284; sums of within-cell distinct counts are respectively 1898/1485 and 2044/1568, not the same statistic. Late panel unions are 972/724 versus 1042/776. Fragment-excluded Morgan bit-Tanimoto, pooled by within-task/seed pair counts, is Child 0.20202255305312947 over 543335 full pairs versus Parent 0.19760265249872405 over 540155; late values are 0.2532065461147983 over 136877 and 0.24161241158396293 over 133298. Eligible molecules have at least six heavy atoms; fingerprints use radius two and 2048 bits, and no pairs cross tasks, seeds or windows. This is distinct from selector count-Tanimoto. Ordinary amides, ethers, carbonyls and amines make much of the output recognizable medicinal chemistry, but 991 Child proposals contain at least one O–O, O–halogen or N–halogen bond, versus Parent 830; these overlapping motif flags are neither toxicity nor synthetic-accessibility scores. Child motif counts are O–O 263, O–halogen 679 and N–halogen 139; Parent counts are 313, 441 and 106. Crowded rings, hydrazine/thiocarbonyl combinations, aldehydes and hemiaminal-like groups add plausibility concerns in particular examples. Every Child and Parent optimizer string lacks @ tokens. Current matched RDKit perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2437 Child and 2570 Parent rows; the exact perception settings are recorded, and these are new paired descriptor readings rather than substitutions for older reports using other definitions. No stereoisomer preference follows. Neutral strings also do not exclude basic amines. Scores are read from the trajectories only; no objective formula, target pharmacophore, synthesis feasibility, biological activity, safety, mechanism activation or component attribution is inferred. Final trajectory entries are last purchases, not necessarily final incumbents. Candidate timing, origin allocation and changed-choice mediation are outside this chemistry assessment. Provenance: policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/inputs-sha256.json, policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/source-map.json and policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-summary.json. The source map identifies every raw Search file and immutable audit; Child copies preserve the exact bytes of the request-authorized staging files. Published Parent chemistry history was read at nodes/n-b13ef5ae4ba8/molecular.json, with its original n-e4b751133c75 comparison conditions retained below.

liabilities: The hydroperoxy group in C2:259 and imidate-like substituent in C2:297 make stability and preparation uncertain without direct evidence.
Highly fused variants and oversized recombinants can be difficult to prepare even though their molecular graphs are accepted.
missing_features: The informative fused-ring/carbonyl arrangement is not consistently preserved during exploration: the same output contains tiny disconnected-from-the-leader chemotypes and very large assemblies. This is a gap in preserving useful structural relationships, not a shortage of rings.

The upper neighborhood includes peroxide and imidate-like appendages alongside conventional methoxy/ketone chemistry; broader conservative alternatives at those attachment sites remain an opportunity. The trajectories do not identify a specific absent target pharmacophore or prove its benefit.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed higher scores accompany intact, moderately sized fused aromatic carbonyl systems. C0:240 OCl and C2:200 O both score 0.0, while the much larger, 67-heavy-atom ester/thioester/thiocarbonyl assembly C0:275 scores 1.7254613109136346e-64. More rings or more atoms alone therefore do not explain the gradient. C2:228 methoxy and C2:259 hydroperoxy analogues share 0.42097944191608694; the imidate-like C2:297 is higher, but this local association does not establish physical stability or a universally favorable group. The last C2:300 proposal scores 2.6752207069335986e-13 and is not the incumbent.

Upper structures include indole carbonyls, ring-associated amines and fused diones. Some large molecules retain substantial scores while other large assemblies and small fragments do poorly; these are associations, not a universal size law or component attribution. This continues the structural-preservation gap originally reported by n-b13ef5ae4ba8 against n-e4b751133c75 under its own complete Search comparison; that original source and condition are not replaced. Exact current evidence and definitions are in policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/inputs-sha256.json and policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful ring, amine and carbonyl relationships are not reliably maintained while the generator changes molecular size and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make contraction, expansion and scaffold rearrangement capable of retaining informative local donor/acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships. Let current-session accepted feedback determine which structures and sizes are useful. Do not impose a named scaffold, task-specific answer or universal hard size cutoff; these output observations do not isolate a mutation operator or statistical consumer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-fc3b91c9623a under the same complete Search conditions versus n-b13ef5ae4ba8. O–O/O–halogen/N–halogen union counts are 991/4350 versus 830/4350, with 593/2175 versus 500/2175 late. Upper examples include peroxide, N–F, O–F, hydrazine and crowded N/O-containing motifs. An O–F-bearing fused dione and its methoxy analogue have exactly equal stored scores, and other upper structures use ordinary ether, carbonyl and tertiary-amine chemistry. Thus conventional chemistry is not absent; reliable local alternatives and their evaluation are uneven. The earlier gap from n-b13ef5ae4ba8 versus n-e4b751133c75 remains scoped to that original complete Search comparison. Counts are structural flags, not measured stability, synthesis or safety. Sources: policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/inputs-sha256.json, policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-summary.json and nodes/n-b13ef5ae4ba8/molecular.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional local alternatives are reachable but not consistently represented around promising structures containing unusual heteroatom bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide conservative heteroatom, bond and linker substitutions near promising accepted graphs while preserving useful topology, and allow current-session feedback to compare them. Avoid inferring that blanket liability filtering raises the objective or that a high score validates an unusual group. No chemistry association identifies the contribution of the changed algorithm component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-fc3b91c9623a and published n-b13ef5ae4ba8, complete frozen Search panel under the same profile. Neither panel has any @ tokens among 4350 optimizer strings. Under the explicitly recorded current RDKit settings, potential tetrahedral centres occur in 2437 Child rows and 2570 Parent rows, including substituted amino rings, hemiaminal-like centres and oxygen/amino cages. The persistent gap was also reported by n-b13ef5ae4ba8 against n-e4b751133c75 under that report’s descriptor definitions and original comparison; those historical counts are not being redefined. Present trajectories show no measured stereoisomer preference. Sources: policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/inputs-sha256.json, policy/scratch/r0057-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-summary.json and nodes/n-b13ef5ae4ba8/molecular.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not distinguish the tetrahedral stereochemical alternatives created by substituted saturated and bridged ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where compatible with the frozen identity/evaluation contract, preserve and distinguish meaningful stereochemical states produced by de novo graph edits. Use accepted current-session feedback to determine whether they matter; prescribe no configuration and claim no score improvement without a registered measurement.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
